nodes.name: ErrorTrigger
nodes.notes: Layer 1 (improvements 3.7). Every other workflow names this one in settings.errorWorkflow, so any execution that ENDS IN ERROR -- a node threw with no error branch -- lands here with the workflow, the node and the message. An execution the internal handler caught never ends in error and never arrives here; the two deliberate throws that already alert are named in ShapeError and suppressed. n8n does not fire an error workflow for manual test runs, so the proof is the webhook probe (ryvo_error_probe), not the Test button.

nodes.name: ShapeError
nodes.notes: No error branch on purpose: n8n never runs an error workflow for the error workflow, so a throw here is simply a failed execution of the handler, visible in the list.

nodes.name: IsSuppressed
nodes.notes: True only for the two named deliberate throws, which already alerted on their own path.

nodes.name: EmailError
nodes.notes: Email first: the leg that does not expire. Addresses hardcoded on purpose -- an alert target read from the monitored system is gone when it is needed (D1).

nodes.name: NotifyError
nodes.notes: The 'tell me now' leg (3.7 tiers). Target hardcoded like the keepalive's: config.escalate_to lives in Supabase, which may be the thing that failed. Rides the sandbox, so the email is the record.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify((() => { const s = $('ShapeError').first().json; return { client_id: null, type: 'run.errored', severity: 'critical', summary: 'Execution ended in error: ' + s.workflowName + ' at ' + s.node + ' - ' + String(s.message).slice(0, 120), data: { workflow_id: s.workflowId, workflow: s.workflowName, node: s.node, execution_id: s.executionId, execution_url: s.executionUrl, mode: s.mode, message: s.message, at: s.at } }; })()) }}

nodes.name: RecordEvent
nodes.notes: Best effort: the record for the cockpit. Supabase may be what failed, so a refused insert is noted by AssertDelivered and never blocks the alert.
